That girl
THAT gurl
noun phrase (Gen-Z slang)
A TikTok trend of 2020–2021: videos of a young woman’s idealized morning — 5 a.m. alarm, lemon water or green juice, journaling, pilates, skincare, a tidy desk, a planner — captioned "becoming that girl." The phrase predates the trend in ordinary speech ("she’s that girl," the one everyone notices); the trend fixed it to the aspirational wellness routine.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

In current slang that girl is the aspirational young woman who has her life together: up early, hydrated, journaled, exercised, skin perfect, desk aesthetic, goals written down. "Becoming that girl" is a self-improvement project. The Christian observation: discipline is good, and Scripture’s own ideal woman rises early. She "looketh well to the ways of her household, and eateth not the bread of idleness" (Pro 31:27). Jesus Himself, "rising up a great while before day," went to a solitary place "and there prayed" (Mar 1:35). The difference is the centre. That girl’s morning revolves around self-optimization and is performed for a camera; Christ’s morning revolves around the Father and was done in a solitary place. "Take heed that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen of them" (Mat 6:1). And the routine carries a hidden law: if you do not get up at 5 a.m. you have failed. But "It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late... for so he giveth his beloved sleep" (Psa 127:2). A father tells his daughter: rise early if you can, and spend the first hour with God, not your reflection; the woman Scripture praises is busy loving others, not curating herself, and she is praised because she "feareth the LORD" (Pro 31:30).

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen-Z slang (TikTok, 2020–2021) for the aspirational, put-together woman of the filmed morning routine — real discipline aimed at self-optimization; Scripture aims the early hour at God.

THAT GIRL, n. phr. (Gen-Z slang, 2020–present; TikTok) The idealized, disciplined young woman of the wellness morning routine: early rising, green juice, journaling, workouts, skincare. "New year, becoming that girl."

Ordinary-speech sense: the girl everyone notices ("she’s that girl").

Related trends: clean girl, 5 a.m. club, it girl.

Webster (1828), root word girl: “GIRL, noun gerl. [&hellip;] 1. A female child, or young woman. In familiar language, any young unmarried woman. 2. Among sportsmen, a roebuck of two years old.”

Decode for parents: good habits, filmed. Ask who the morning is for.

Key Scripture

Mar 1:35 — "And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed."

Pro 31:27 — "She looketh well to the ways of her household, and eateth not the bread of idleness."

Mat 6:1 — "Take heed that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise ye have no reward of your Father which is in heaven."

Psa 127:2 — "It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so he giveth his beloved sleep."

Pro 31:30 — "Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised."

Modern Corruption

That girl dresses self-optimization as virtue and performs it for an audience; Scripture commends early discipline but centres it on prayer in secret and on serving others.

expand to see more

The trend borrows the shape of a godly morning and removes the God. Early rising, order, and diligence are commended in Proverbs 31; the problem is the axis. Every element of the "that girl" morning returns to the self — my skin, my body, my goals, my aesthetic — and the whole thing is filmed. Jesus warned against piety performed "to be seen of them" (Mat 6:1); self-improvement performed to be seen is the same reward, collected early.

It also lays a quiet law on girls who cannot keep it. Miss the 5 a.m. alarm and you are not that girl. Psalm 127 lifts that weight: it is vain to rise early in anxious striving, "for so he giveth his beloved sleep." Teach your daughter Mark 1:35 — the early hour alone with the Father — and Proverbs 31:30: the praised woman is the one who fears the LORD.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Ordinary "she’s that girl" → 2020–2021 TikTok "becoming that girl" morning-routine trend → general label for the disciplined, aesthetic, self-optimizing young woman.
